bull.t: Improved cash generation (OCF and FCF positive)
bull.b: Sustained positive operating cash flow and free cash flow provide durable funding for operations, bolt‑on M&A, and buybacks without immediate reliance on equity. Over 2–6 months this supports liquidity and execution of strategic initiatives even if revenue is volatile.

bull.t: Margin expansion and record adjusted EBITDA outlook
bull.b: Ongoing cost optimization and operating efficiencies have driven margin expansion and a record EBITDA target, which indicates structural improvements in operating leverage. Better margins increase cash conversion and resilience to topline shocks over the medium term.

bull.t: Predictable testing business and visible project backlog
bull.b: A visible backlog in testing and Consulting & Treatment provides predictable revenue cadence and supports margin stability. High‑quality projects reduce revenue volatility from episodic emergency work, aiding durable cash flow visibility over upcoming quarters.

bear.b: Material revenue decline and a sizable guidance cut reflect weaker demand in emergency response and pass‑through activity. Persistent topline pressure reduces operating leverage and makes margin gains harder to sustain absent a return to historical revenue levels.

bear.t: Rising leverage and persistently negative ROE
bear.b: Higher leverage increases financial risk and interest burden, limiting strategic flexibility. Combined with negative ROE, the capital base is not yet producing consistent shareholder returns, amplifying earnings volatility if operating momentum stalls.

bear.t: Board strategic review and shareholder protections increase uncertainty
bear.b: A board‑led strategic review and anti‑takeover rights plan signal potential portfolio changes or transactions but create execution and timeline uncertainty. This can delay capital allocation decisions and introduce strategic risk over the medium term.
